backlog.spec: In featurize, besides the Morgan bits, append the full RDKit 2D descriptor vector from rdkit.Chem.Descriptors.CalcMolDescriptors (or the list Descriptors._descList). Replace any NaN or inf values with 0 and clip extreme values to the 1st-99th percentile range of the training set. Keep the rest of the random forest unchanged. Descriptors such as MolLogP, TPSA and HBD/HBA are strongly tied to logD and should help the trees generalise across scaffolds.
backlog.title: Add RDKit physchem descriptors to fingerprints

backlog.spec: Build a compact 6-column descriptor block per molecule: Crippen MolLogP, TPSA, molecular weight, number of HBD, number of HBA and number of rotatable bonds. Concatenate it to the 2048-bit Morgan fingerprint before fitting the random forest. Because the forest picks features at random, use max_features as before but make sure these dense columns are included in the candidate pool. This is a cheap test of whether a few strong physchem priors beat the raw bit vector.
backlog.title: Crippen logP and TPSA as a small descriptor block

backlog.spec: Replace the bit-vector Morgan fingerprint with a count fingerprint: use gen.GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy with the same radius 2 and 2048 size. Counts keep information about repeated substructures, such as multiple polar groups, that a bit vector collapses. Leave the random forest hyperparameters unchanged so the only change is the representation.
backlog.title: Count-based Morgan fingerprints instead of bits

backlog.spec: Compute a second Morgan fingerprint with the feature-invariant atom typing, rdFingerprintGenerator.GetMorganGenerator(radius=2, fpSize=1024, atomInvariantsGenerator=GetMorganFeatureAtomInvGen()). Concatenate it with the standard 1024-bit ECFP fingerprint. The feature variant groups donors, acceptors, aromatic and ionisable atoms, which generalises better across unseen scaffolds than pure atom identity.
backlog.title: Add FCFP-style feature-invariant Morgan fingerprints

backlog.spec: Add two more fingerprints beside Morgan: an atom-pair count fingerprint (rdFingerprintGenerator.GetAtomPairGenerator, 1024 bits, counts) and a topological torsion count fingerprint (GetTopologicalTorsionGenerator, 512 bits). Concatenate them with the Morgan vector and fit the same random forest. These capture long-range shape and polarity patterns that circular fingerprints miss.
backlog.title: Atom-pair and topological-torsion fingerprints

backlog.spec: Append the 167-bit MACCS key fingerprint (rdkit.Chem.MACCSkeys.GenMACCSKeys, converted to a numpy array) to the Morgan features. MACCS encodes general functional-group presence that is useful for logD, where ionisable and polar groups dominate. Keep the random forest settings unchanged.
backlog.title: MACCS keys as an extra block

backlog.spec: Add a small set of hand-written SMARTS counts to the features: carboxylic acid, tetrazole, acyl sulfonamide (acidic), aliphatic amine (tertiary, secondary, primary, basic), amidine and guanidine, quaternary nitrogen, and phenol. logD depends strongly on ionisation at pH 7.4, so these counts give the model a direct handle on it. Append them as integer columns to the Morgan fingerprint.
backlog.title: Ionisable-group count features

backlog.spec: Replace RandomForestRegressor with lightgbm.LGBMRegressor using objective='l1' so it optimises mean absolute error directly, which is the scoring metric. Use about 800 trees, learning_rate 0.03, num_leaves 31, min_child_samples 10, feature_fraction 0.3, bagging_fraction 0.8 with bagging_freq 1, and random_state=seed, with n_jobs=8. Keep the same Morgan fingerprint featurisation.
backlog.title: Switch the random forest to LightGBM with L1 objective

backlog.spec: Replace the forest with xgboost.XGBRegressor, objective 'reg:pseudohubererror' with huber_slope 0.5, max_depth 6, learning_rate 0.05, 600 rounds, subsample 0.8, colsample_bytree 0.3, min_child_weight 3 and random_state=seed. The Huber loss is robust to the outliers that are common in measured logD values and behaves like MAE on large residuals, while staying smooth for gradient boosting.
backlog.title: XGBoost with pseudo-Huber loss on the fingerprints

backlog.spec: Replace the forest with catboost.CatBoostRegressor, loss_function 'MAE', 1000 iterations, learning_rate 0.05, depth 6, l2_leaf_reg 3, random_seed=seed, verbose False, thread_count 8. Feed it the Morgan count features. CatBoost's ordered boosting and symmetric trees are often strong on small tabular data with high-dimensional sparse inputs.
backlog.title: CatBoost on count fingerprints

backlog.spec: Compute Tanimoto similarity between Morgan bit-vectors for train and test (K = A·B / (|A|+|B|-A·B) using the dot products of the 0/1 numpy arrays). Fit a kernel ridge regressor (sklearn KernelRidge with kernel='precomputed') on the training Gram matrix, with alpha tuned on a small grid of [0.01, 0.1, 1.0] using an inner 5-fold split of the training data. Predict test values from the test-to-train Tanimoto matrix. Similarity kernels are the standard strong baseline for fingerprint regression.
backlog.title: Gaussian process with Tanimoto kernel

backlog.spec: Use sklearn SVR with kernel='precomputed', where the Gram matrix is the Tanimoto similarity between Morgan bit-vectors (K = A·B / (|A|+|B|-A·B)). Set epsilon=0.1, C=5.0. Targets are used as is. The epsilon-insensitive loss is close to the MAE objective and the Tanimoto kernel captures structural similarity directly. Compare with the random forest by keeping the same featurisation for the kernel.
backlog.title: Support vector regression with Tanimoto kernel

backlog.spec: Train a sklearn MLPRegressor on the Morgan bit or count vector: hidden_layer_sizes (512, 128), activation 'relu', alpha 1e-3 (L2), learning_rate_init 1e-3, early_stopping=True with validation_fraction 0.15, max_iter 300, random_state=seed. Standardise the target with the training mean and standard deviation before fitting and invert the transform on the predictions. Neural nets on fingerprints can complement the tree models.
backlog.title: Deep MLP on fingerprints with dropout

backlog.spec: Predict each test molecule as the similarity-weighted mean of its k nearest training neighbours under Tanimoto similarity on Morgan bit-vectors. Use k=10, weights proportional to similarity raised to power 3. This is a non-parametric baseline that often transfers well across scaffolds. Return the predictions directly without any learned model.
backlog.title: k-nearest-neighbour Tanimoto regression

backlog.spec: Fit both the existing random forest and a LightGBM regressor with objective 'l1' on the same features, then return the arithmetic mean of their two predictions on the test set. Averaging a bagged model with a boosted model usually reduces variance more than either alone. Both models use random_state=seed.
backlog.title: Average of random forest and LightGBM predictions

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, run 5-fold out-of-fold predictions on the training set for three base learners: random forest, LightGBM with L1 objective, and Tanimoto kernel ridge. Fit a non-negative least-absolute-deviation style blend, or simply a sklearn Ridge with positive=True, on the stacked out-of-fold predictions to get the blend weights. Refit each base learner on all training data and apply the weights to the test predictions. Use seed for all fold splits.
backlog.title: Stacked ensemble with a ridge meta-learner

backlog.spec: Sweep min_samples_leaf over {1, 3, 5} and max_features over {0.2, 0.3, 0.5} for the random forest with 500 trees. Pick the pair with the lowest out-of-bag mean absolute error (use oob_score=True, but compute MAE from oob_prediction_ yourself, since the built-in score is R^2). Refit on all training data with the chosen pair and random_state=seed. This keeps the model family but tunes the bias-variance balance.
backlog.title: Random forest with deeper trees and min_samples_leaf tuning

backlog.spec: Instead of the mean of the forest trees, compute the per-tree predictions with np.stack([t.predict(X) for t in model.estimators_]) and return the median over trees. The median is less influenced by a few trees that extrapolate badly to unseen scaffolds and approximates an MAE-optimal central estimate. Keep the random forest training unchanged.
backlog.title: Bagging of forests with a median-of-trees aggregate

backlog.spec: Before fitting, transform the training target with y' = sign(y) * log1p(|y|) and fit the model on y'. Invert on the predictions with sign(p)*expm1(|p|). Logd values are roughly centred but have a heavy tail, so the transform can reduce the influence of extreme measurements on the squared-error splits. Use the existing random forest otherwise.
backlog.title: Target transformation with a signed log

backlog.spec: Clip the training targets to the 1st and 99th percentile of train_y before fitting the model, and keep the test predictions unclipped. Measured logD values include a few extreme points that pull tree leaves and split criteria off-centre. Clipping reduces this influence without removing any molecules. Use the existing random forest and the same fingerprint.
backlog.title: Winsorise extreme training targets

backlog.spec: Compute the Bemis-Murcko scaffold of each training molecule and weight each sample by the inverse square root of how many training molecules share its scaffold. This stops over-represented scaffold families from dominating the fit, which matters because the test folds hold out whole scaffolds. Pass the weights as sample_weight to the random forest fit.
backlog.title: Scaffold-aware sample weighting

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, train the random forest with three different random states derived from seed (seed, seed+1, seed+2) with 200 trees each, and average the three prediction vectors. This reduces the variance from bootstrap and feature sampling beyond what a single 300-tree forest achieves. Keep the total fit time well under the time limit, since 15 fits must finish in 10 minutes.
backlog.title: Multi-seed averaging within fit_predict

backlog.spec: After featurisation, drop all Morgan bit columns that are set in fewer than 5 or more than 95 percent of training molecules, computed on the training data only. Apply the same column mask to the test features. Removing near-constant and near-universal bits reduces noise for the random forest's feature sampling and speeds up fitting. Keep the forest settings unchanged.
backlog.title: Feature selection by variance and frequency

backlog.spec: Change the Morgan generator to radius 3 with fpSize 4096 and keep the rest of the random forest pipeline. Larger radius encodes wider chemical environments, and the bigger vector reduces bit collisions. Check the runtime: the forest's max_features=0.3 will now scan more columns, so reduce N_TREES to 200 if needed to stay within the time budget.
backlog.title: Larger fingerprint radius and bit count

backlog.spec: Compute the full RDKit 2D descriptor set plus the Morgan bits, and fit the random forest on this combined matrix with max_features=0.2 to keep split candidates diverse. Impute NaN and inf values with the training column median. The dense descriptor columns give the trees direct access to lipophilicity-related quantities without relying on many sparse bit splits.
backlog.title: Hybrid of descriptors and the forest with feature bagging

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, run a small random search of 12 configurations for the LightGBM L1 model over num_leaves in {15, 31, 63}, min_child_samples in {5, 10, 20}, feature_fraction in {0.2, 0.4}, and learning_rate 0.03 with 600 rounds. Score each configuration by a 4-fold inner group split using the training scaffolds as groups (GroupKFold on Murcko scaffold strings), and keep the best. Refit on all training data with random_state=seed.
backlog.title: Partial-dependence-free hyperparameter tuning of LightGBM

backlog.spec: For the LightGBM L1 model, hold out 10 percent of the training molecules, grouped by Murcko scaffold, as a validation set. Train with a large number of rounds (up to 2000, learning_rate 0.03) and early stopping on the validation L1 with patience 100. Then refit on the full training set using the best iteration count scaled by 1.1. Early stopping prevents the boosted model from overfitting to scaffold-specific patterns.
backlog.title: Early stopping for boosted models via inner validation

backlog.spec: Use LightGBM with objective 'l1' and a learning-rate schedule that decays from 0.08 to 0.01 across 1000 rounds, implemented with the callbacks reset_parameter and a linear function of the iteration index. Keep num_leaves 31 and feature_fraction 0.3. A decaying step size lets early trees fit the broad trend fast and later trees refine the residuals with smaller steps.
backlog.title: Learning-rate decay schedule for gradient boosting

backlog.spec: Use LightGBM with objective 'l1', bagging_fraction 0.6 with bagging_freq 1, feature_fraction 0.2, and lambda_l2 of 5.0, with 1000 rounds at learning_rate 0.02. Stronger row and column subsampling acts as regularisation against scaffold-specific memorisation, which is the main failure mode when test scaffolds are unseen. Set random_state=seed.
backlog.title: Subsampled boosting with row and column dropout

backlog.spec: Train three LightGBM models with objective 'quantile' at alpha 0.4, 0.5 and 0.6, all with random_state=seed. Return the average of the three predictions. Averaging neighbouring quantiles smooths the median estimate and is a cheap way to approximate an MAE-optimal central prediction with less variance than a single model.
backlog.title: Quantile-averaged gradient boosting

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, after the usual base_predict stack produces test predictions, take the test molecules whose stacked predictions agree most across the three base learners (lowest spread, e.g. the 50% with smallest std across columns) and append them to the training set with their predicted values as pseudo-labels. Refit the stack on the augmented set (same GroupKFold OOF procedure, same seed) and predict the test set again. Keep the pseudo-labelled rows out of the OOF targets so the meta-learner is fit only on real labels. Use only the seed argument for randomness.
backlog.title: Transductive pseudo-label self-training

backlog.spec: Add a small block of 3D shape descriptors per molecule: embed one conformer with rdDistGeom.ETKDGv3 (fixed randomSeed=seed, maxAttempts limited, fall back to zeros if embedding fails), then compute rdMolDescriptors.CalcPBF, CalcNPR1, CalcNPR2, CalcRadiusOfGyration, CalcInertialShapeFactor and CalcEccentricity. Cache per SMILES like desc_vector, clip to the 1st-99th percentile of the training block, and append the six columns to the tree-model input matrix Xtr/Xte only. Leave the Tanimoto kernel unchanged.
backlog.title: 3D shape descriptors from ETKDG conformers

backlog.spec: Replace the Tanimoto-only kernel ridge member with a sum of two kernels: the existing Tanimoto kernel on ECFP bits, and an RBF kernel exp(-gamma * ||z_i - z_j||^2) on standardized RDKit descriptor vectors (z-scored with training-fold mean and std, clipped to the 1st-99th percentiles, gamma = 1/(n_descriptors * 2)). Use K = K_tanimoto + K_rbf, solve (K + lambda I) w = y - mu with lambda = 0.5, and predict test rows with the same combined kernel. Keep the other two base learners and the Ridge meta-learner unchanged.
backlog.title: Combined Tanimoto plus RBF kernel ridge base learner

backlog.spec: Compute for each training molecule its neighbourhood density as the count of other training molecules with ECFP Tanimoto similarity at least 0.5, computed inside the training fold only. Set sample weight = 1 / sqrt(1 + density), normalised to mean 1, and pass it as weight= to the LightGBM Dataset and to RandomForestRegressor.fit (sample_weight=). This down-weights over-represented chemical series so that the models spend capacity on sparse regions. Kernel ridge stays unweighted. The weights are computed independently in each call to base_predict, from the training rows passed in.
backlog.title: Density-based training sample weights

backlog.spec: Make the LightGBM base learner a residual model: for the training rows, use the out-of-fold Tanimoto kernel ridge predictions from an inner GroupKFold (5 folds, by scaffold) as a feature column, and train LightGBM L1 on the target y minus that feature, with the same Morgan plus descriptor matrix. At prediction time, compute the kernel ridge prediction for the test rows from a model fit on all training rows, add the LightGBM residual, and return the sum as this base learner's output. Keep the random forest and the Ridge meta-learner unchanged.
backlog.title: Residual boosting on out-of-fold kernel predictions

backlog.spec: After the Ridge meta-learner produces OOF stacked predictions (meta_oof = meta fitted on oof, evaluated by the same OOF scheme), fit a monotone calibration from the stacked score to the target using sklearn IsotonicRegression(out_of_bounds='clip') on the OOF pairs (meta_oof, y). Apply this isotonic map to the final test prediction from meta.predict(base_te). Its purpose is to correct shrinkage at the tails that a linear meta-learner leaves in place. Leave everything else in the pipeline unchanged.
backlog.title: Post-stack isotonic recalibration of predictions

backlog.spec: Replace the positive Ridge meta-learner with an explicit mean-absolute-error fit: find non-negative weights w (one per base learner, plus an intercept b restricted to the range of y) that minimise sum |y_i - (oof_i @ w + b)| subject to w >= 0 and sum(w) = 1. Solve it as a linear program with scipy.optimize.linprog (HiGHS), using slack variables for the absolute values. Use the OOF predictions as the design matrix and apply the solved weights to the base learners' test predictions. Fall back to the simple average if the solver fails.
backlog.title: L1-optimal convex meta-learner via linear programming

backlog.spec: Change the LightGBM base learner to boosting_type='dart' with L1 objective, drop_rate=0.1, skip_drop=0.5, max_drop=50, and num_boost_round set to 400 because DART is slower per round. Keep learning_rate=0.03, num_leaves=31, min_child_samples=10 and feature_fraction=0.2. Use the seed argument in the params so the drop choices are reproducible. The rest of the stack and the Ridge meta-learner stay unchanged. Watch the 10-minute limit, since DART costs more per round than gbdt.
backlog.title: DART boosting for the LightGBM base learner

backlog.spec: Add a hashed count vector of BRICS fragments: for each molecule, call BRICSDecompose on the parent molecule to get fragment SMILES, hash each fragment string into 512 buckets with a deterministic hash (zlib.crc32 modulo 512, not Python's hash), and count occurrences. Append these 512 count columns to the Morgan plus descriptor matrix used by the tree models only, after the same 1st-99th percentile clipping as the descriptors. Keep the Tanimoto kernel on the ECFP bits, unchanged.
backlog.title: Fragment-count features from BRICS decomposition

backlog.spec: Wrap the whole stacked pipeline in K=5 row-bagged replicas: each replica draws a bootstrap sample of the training rows (with replacement, rng seeded from the seed argument plus the replica index), runs the complete OOF stack (GroupKFold inside the bag, same base learners and Ridge meta-learner), and predicts the test set. Return the element-wise median of the five test predictions. Use this to reduce variance from the single ensemble run. Check that the job still fits inside the 10-minute limit, and drop to K=3 if it does not.
backlog.title: Row-bagged ensemble of the stack with median aggregation

backlog.spec: In fit_predict, before any featurisation or descriptor computation, pass every SMILES through a standardisation step: parse with Chem.MolFromSmiles, keep only the largest fragment (rdkit.Chem.rdMolStandardize.LargestFragmentChooser), and neutralise charges with rdMolStandardize.Uncharger. Use the standardised SMILES everywhere (featurize, desc_vector, and the Murcko scaffold groups). Keep the cache keyed by the standardised string. Nothing else changes.
backlog.title: Salt stripping and charge neutralisation before featurising

backlog.spec: Before the base learners are fit, compute Crippen MolLogP for each training molecule (Descriptors.MolLogP, cached like desc_vector). Fit a one-variable least-squares line y ~ a + b*MolLogP on the training fold only, and train all three base learners and the kernel member on the residual r = y - (a + b*MolLogP). At prediction time add the same baseline back for the test molecules before the meta-learner. The meta-learner still sees the raw-scale base predictions, so keep the stacking code as is.
backlog.title: Crippen logP residual target

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, after the inner GroupKFold loop has produced oof for the single-model LightGBM member, compute the absolute OOF residual of each training row. Train the final base_predict models in two stages: first on the 70% of rows with the smallest residuals, then on all rows, warm-starting LightGBM with init_model or, for the kernel ridge member, by adding the remaining rows with weight 0.5 to a second solve. Keep the same number of rounds and hyperparameters. The goal is to let easy molecules shape the fit before the noisy ones.
backlog.title: Curriculum by out-of-fold error

backlog.spec: Replace the single LightGBM fit in base_predict with one training run of 600 rounds, from which predictions are taken at rounds 200, 400 and 600 using m.predict(Xb, num_iteration=k). Average those three predictions to form p_lgb. The member then carries an implicit learning-rate schedule. The rest of base_predict and the meta-learner are unchanged.
backlog.title: Snapshot averaging of LightGBM across the learning curve

backlog.spec: In the kernel ridge member, replace the single ECFP Tanimoto kernel with the sum of three Tanimoto kernels, computed on ECFP radius 1 with 1024 bits, ECFP radius 2 with 1024 bits, and the atom-pair count fingerprint (1024 bits, count vectors, using the min/sum Tanimoto form). Keep the RBF term on the standardised descriptors and divide the summed kernel by 3 so the regularisation scale is unchanged. Compute all three kernels from the same cached arrays, and keep the solve with 0.5 * I.
backlog.title: Multiple-kernel Tanimoto sum over several fingerprint types

backlog.spec: Inside base_predict, for the kernel ridge member only, grid-search two values: the ridge lambda in {0.1, 0.5, 2.0} and the RBF weight in {0.5, 1.0, 2.0} that multiplies rbf in K. Pick the pair with the lowest MAE on a 4-fold GroupKFold split of the training rows (groups = Murcko scaffolds passed in from fit_predict). Refit the kernel on all rows with the chosen pair and predict. The LightGBM and RF members keep their current settings. This is a cheap solve, since the 1000-row kernel solve is fast.
backlog.title: Inner-CV tuning of kernel ridge regularisation and kernel mixing

backlog.spec: Replace the row-based inner loop with a group bootstrap: draw 5 bootstrap samples of the training scaffolds (sample group labels with replacement, then take every row whose scaffold was drawn). For each sample, fit the full base_predict and record predictions on the out-of-bag rows (rows whose scaffolds were not drawn). Use the out-of-bag predictions as the stack's training matrix for the meta-learner, and average the 5 fitted models' predictions on the test set as the base test output. Keep the meta-learner Ridge(alpha=1e-3, positive=True).
backlog.title: Scaffold-group bootstrap of the whole stack

backlog.spec: For the random forest and LightGBM members only, create two augmented copies of the training matrix Xa in which each fingerprint bit (the first 2*N_BITS columns) is zeroed independently with probability 0.1, and stack them with the original rows, keeping the labels duplicated. Fit both models on the augmented matrix. At prediction time, average the predictions over the clean test matrix and three copies with 10% of fingerprint bits zeroed using a fixed seed. The kernel member is unchanged.
backlog.title: Bit-dropout augmentation with test-time averaging

backlog.spec: After the inner loop produces oof for the stacking, form soft targets y_soft = 0.7 * y + 0.3 * (meta-learner's OOF prediction) on the training rows. Refit the whole stack, using y_soft as the training target for the three base learners but the true y for the meta-learner fit. Predict test molecules with the refitted base learners through the same meta-learner. The goal is to smooth noisy labels with the consensus of the other models, in the spirit of self-distillation.
backlog.title: Self-distillation of training targets from out-of-fold predictions

backlog.spec: Add a fourth base learner to base_predict: an ElasticNet (sklearn, alpha=0.01, l1_ratio=0.5, max_iter=5000) fit on the standardised RDKit descriptor columns (the last 200-odd columns of Xa, z-scored using training-fold statistics) concatenated with the ECFP and FCFP bit columns. Return its prediction as an additional column of the oof matrix so the Ridge meta-learner blends it with the other three. The linear member is cheap and is a different inductive bias from the forest, boosting and kernel members.
backlog.title: Sparse elastic-net member on standardised descriptors and count features

backlog.spec: Add a hashed Weisfeiler-Lehman subtree count vector as an extra feature block. For each molecule, start from atom invariants (element, degree, formal charge, aromaticity, H count), run 3 WL refinement iterations over the heavy-atom graph, and hash each (iteration, label) pair with zlib.crc32 into 1024 buckets. Count occurrences per bucket and append the vector to the existing Morgan plus descriptor matrix. Leave the Tanimoto kernel on ECFP bits only. Use the same featurisation for train and test so nothing leaks across folds.
backlog.title: Weisfeiler-Lehman subtree count features

backlog.spec: Compute the ring-only generic Murcko scaffold (all atoms set to carbon, all bonds single) for every molecule. Inside fit_predict, build a target-encoded feature: for each molecule, the mean training label of other molecules sharing its generic scaffold, shrunk toward the global mean with pseudo-count 5. Compute this encoding out-of-fold within the training set so the feature never sees the molecule's own label, and for test molecules use all training labels. Append the single column to the descriptor block fed to the LightGBM and random forest base learners.
backlog.title: Generic-scaffold target encoding

backlog.spec: Replace the squared-error kernel ridge member with an absolute-error version fitted by iteratively reweighted least squares. Start from the current Tanimoto plus RBF kernel solution. At each of about 15 iterations, set per-sample weights w_i = 1 / max(|residual_i|, 0.05), solve the weighted system (K + lambda W^-1) alpha = y - mu, and recompute residuals. Keep the same lambda and RBF weight grid search, using the held-out MAE as the selection criterion. This targets the MAE metric directly rather than the squared error the member currently minimises.
backlog.title: IRLS L1-loss kernel regression member

backlog.spec: Add a second kernel-ridge member whose kernel is the elementwise product of the Tanimoto ECFP kernel and the RBF kernel on standardised descriptors, K = T * R, instead of their sum. Keep the existing sum-kernel member and feed both predictions to the stack as separate columns. Use lambda from the same small grid, chosen by the existing inner grouped CV. The product kernel only gives high similarity when both fingerprint and property profiles agree, which is a different inductive bias from the sum.
backlog.title: Product kernel as an alternative kernel member

backlog.spec: Replace the inner grouped-CV grid search for the kernel ridge member with a Gaussian process marginal-likelihood criterion. Eigendecompose the training kernel matrix K = T + wr*R once per wr value. For each lambda on a fixed log-spaced grid, compute the log marginal likelihood of the targets under a zero-mean Gaussian with noise variance lambda, using the eigenvalues and projected targets. Pick the (lambda, wr) pair with the highest likelihood and fit the final weights from that pair. This costs one eigendecomposition per wr value instead of a grid of solves per fold, which keeps the runtime well inside the time limit.
backlog.title: Marginal-likelihood selection of kernel ridge hyperparameters

backlog.spec: Before fitting the LightGBM base learner, augment its training set with mixup. Draw one mixing coefficient per synthetic row from Beta(0.2, 0.2) using the job seed, pair each training row with a random partner from the same training fold, and form convex combinations of both the feature rows and the targets. Append these synthetic rows to the real ones, giving roughly twice as many rows, then train the L1 LightGBM as before. Keep the random forest and kernel members on the un-augmented data so only the boosted member changes.
backlog.title: Mixup augmentation for the LightGBM member

backlog.spec: Train the LightGBM base learner in two stages. Stage one uses the Huber objective with delta set to the median absolute deviation of the training targets and runs 400 rounds to learn a smooth, robust fit. Stage two continues boosting from that model (init_model or raw score init) with the regression_l1 objective for another 300 rounds at a lower learning rate of 0.01. The schedule starts with the stable loss and ends on the metric the harness scores. Keep the same leaves, min_child_samples and feature_fraction settings as the current incumbent member.
backlog.title: Huber-to-L1 annealed LightGBM

backlog.spec: Add a transductive smoothing step on top of the stacked prediction. Build a kNN graph (k=10, Tanimoto similarity on ECFP bits) over the union of training and test molecules inside fit_predict. Run label propagation: initialise the training nodes with their known labels and the test nodes with the stack's predictions, then iterate F <- (1-a)*F0 + a*S*F for about 20 steps with a=0.3, where S is the row-normalised graph. Clamp training rows to their true labels at each step. Return the propagated values for the test molecules. Only use the test-set predictions as the initial values, so nothing from the held-out labels is used.
backlog.title: Label propagation over a transductive Tanimoto graph

backlog.spec: Split the training molecules into two experts by heavy-atom count, using the training median as the cut. Fit a full base_predict stack and meta-learner separately on the small-molecule group and on the large-molecule group. At prediction time, route each test molecule to the expert matching its heavy-atom count, with the global median used for the cut. If one group has fewer than 150 training molecules, fall back to the single stack. The aim is to let the kernel and tree members specialise on the size regimes where lipophilicity drivers differ.
backlog.title: Size-gated mixture of two stacks

backlog.spec: Address the O(n^3) cost of the kernel member by subagging it. Randomly partition the training rows, using the seed, into 4 disjoint blocks stratified by target quantile. Fit the Tanimoto plus RBF kernel ridge member on each block separately, with a fixed lambda and RBF weight taken from the current inner-CV choice. Average the four predictions on the test rows to produce the kernel column for the stack. This cuts the solve cost by about 16x, which frees time for a larger LightGBM grid, and the averaging adds some variance reduction.
backlog.title: Subagged kernel members on disjoint row blocks

incumbent.description: Grid-search the kernel ridge lambda (0.1, 0.5, 2.0) and RBF weight (0.5, 1.0, 2.0) with a 4-fold scaffold-grouped inner CV inside base_predict, then refit the kernel ridge member on all rows with the best pair.

memo: Helped: RDKit 2D descriptors (0.7230 to 0.5902), LightGBM with a cheap inner grid (0.5728), FCFP-style Morgan (0.5585), stacking RF, LightGBM and a Tanimoto kernel learner (0.5357), summed Tanimoto+RBF kernel ridge member (0.5062), then grid-searching its lambda and RBF weight (0.4895, incumbent, only 1 run). Did not help: bit filtering (0.7555), bigger Morgan (0.5880), MLP (0.5719), extra fingerprints/counts (MACCS, atom-pair, BRICS, count FPs 0.5087), ionisable SMARTS, 3D descriptors, density weighting (0.5089), xgboost swap (0.5025), DART (0.4914), label propagation (0.5230), product kernel (0.4895, no change), residual linear model (0.4859, within noise). Heavy inner loops caused timeouts and crashes, so watch the 10-minute limit. Next: replicate the incumbent to confirm 0.4895. Then try a better meta-learner or kernel hyperparameters (RBF gamma). Avoid more feature additions and small tweaks.
